# ADR 0019 — The asset pipeline is an app of the hexagon

> **In short.** In the context of the office assets that are made in Blender and drawn in the browser, facing a
> generator that would otherwise grow as a loose script beside the architecture, we decided to split it along the
> hexagon, with its own app, and against a standalone build script, to keep what an asset is testable and shared with
> the office, accepting one more workspace package.

## Context and problem

Characters and furniture are made in Blender and rendered into office assets (maintainer's vision). Spike PIX-11
decides how; story PIX-25 builds the pipeline. ADR 0011 names three apps, `server`, `client` and `web`; a generator
has no place there yet. The office needs the same facts about an asset that the generator produces: its footprint in
tiles for depth sorting and walking, its anchor, its layers and color slots for characters and furniture that can be
recolored. Later, an asset viewer is to show every asset with its textures and colors.

## Decision drivers

- The generator must not break out of the architecture (maintainer, 2026-10-04).
- What an asset is has to be the same for the generator, the office and a later asset viewer.
- Only one place may know Blender, so another tool can replace it.

## Considered options

- **A — An app of the hexagon:** the asset model in the core, the Blender adapter in infrastructure, the manifest in
  protocol, a seventh workspace package `apps/asset-pipeline` that wires them.
- **B — A standalone build script** under `scripts/` that calls Blender and writes files.

## Decision

Chosen: **A**, because only it keeps the asset model in one tested place that the office and the generator share.

1. **What an asset is lives in the core.** Kind, footprint in tiles, anchor, directions, animations, layers, color
   slots and texture variants are domain types in `packages/core`, with the use case that builds and validates an
   asset set and the ports for rendering and storing it. `[Lint import zones]`
2. **Only an adapter knows Blender.** The headless Blender call and its script live in `packages/infrastructure`
   behind the core's rendering port; the core never starts a process. `[Lint import zones · Hook architecture-guard]`
3. **The browser reads assets only through the manifest.** The manifest's shape is a schema in `packages/protocol`;
   it carries layers, color slots and texture variants as data, so a viewer can show any combination without the core
   and without a new render. `[Lint import zones]`
4. **`apps/asset-pipeline` is the composition root.** It is a workspace package like the other apps and stands under
   the same import zones. `[Config pnpm-workspace.yaml · Lint import zones]`

### Consequences

- Good, because a planted Blender or process call in the core turns lint red from the first line on.
- Good, because the office and the generator cannot disagree about a footprint or a color slot.
- Bad, because a generator needs a port, an adapter and an app instead of one script.

### Confirmation

The import-zone probe of PIX-7 turns red on `node:child_process` in the core and green on
`apps/asset-pipeline` importing infrastructure; PIX-25 tests the asset model in the core with fakes.

## Rejected

- **B — a standalone build script.** It would hold its own idea of an asset beside the office's, untested by the
  core's fakes and outside every import zone.
